skill.name: happyhorse-1-0
skill.description: Use HappyHorse 1.0 on RunComfy to generate short text-to-video clips with synchronized audio. The skill documents inputs, prompts, model limits, CLI invocation, and output handling.
skill.summary: Generate short HappyHorse 1.0 videos on RunComfy from structured text prompts.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick hits are Markdown examples, prompt samples, or inline parameter names, not Ruby execution. The meaningful risks are the intended RunComfy CLI execution, third-party API calls with a bearer token, output downloads, and disclosed token setup.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running runcomfy commands, and show the exact inputs, endpoint, and output directory.
Pin the RunComfy CLI version in installation instructions, and prefer documented package integrity checks when available.
Tell users that prompts and generated assets are sent to RunComfy, and advise against submitting sensitive content.
Keep token file permissions at 0600, document token rotation, and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI environments.
Keep the download host whitelist and file size cap, and write only to a user-approved output directory.

content.value_statement: Short video prompts often miss motion, audio, and model limits. This skill guides HappyHorse 1.0 setup, prompt design, and RunComfy CLI execution.
actual_capabilities: Documents the HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video endpoint and supported input fields.
Shows RunComfy CLI commands for default, vertical, and low-cost test generations.
Explains prompt patterns for motion, camera framing, multi-shot consistency, and audio direction.
Lists supported aspect ratios, resolutions, durations, seed behavior, and watermark control.
Describes CLI polling, result download behavior, exit codes, and token storage.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account and local RunComfy CLI installation.
Covers text-to-video only; image-to-video requires a separate pipeline.
Generated clips are limited to the documented 3 to 15 second duration range.
External audio cannot be supplied for lip-sync through this template.

use_cases.title: Create Short Brand Videos
use_cases.description: Plan prompt settings for short 1080P video clips with motion, camera language, and ambient sound.

use_cases.title: Build Vertical Social Clips
use_cases.description: Generate platform-ready vertical prompts with duration, aspect ratio, watermark, and audio choices.

use_cases.title: Test Video Model Fit
use_cases.description: Compare HappyHorse 1.0 with sibling models when a brief needs lip-sync, references, or longer motion control.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple text-to-video generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use HappyHorse 1.0 to create a 5 second 16:9 1080P clip about [scene]. Include clear motion and ambient audio.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Vertical Short
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for social video format control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 HappyHorse 1.0 short for [platform]. Use 8 seconds, one main action, and audio that supports the scene.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Shot Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for character consistency across two beats.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a two-shot HappyHorse 1.0 prompt about [story]. Restate the same character, clothing, location, camera style, and audio in each shot.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this video brief: [brief]. Decide whether HappyHorse 1.0 fits, name any limits, and prepare the RunComfy generation settings.

output_examples.input: Generate a vertical product teaser for a cafe drink.
output_examples.output: Recommended settings: 9:16, 8 seconds, 1080P, watermark enabled. Prompt focus: close-up pour, visible steam, warm cafe ambience, and one clear camera move.

output_examples.input: Create a two-shot story with one consistent character.
output_examples.output: The response restates the same character and wardrobe in both shots, then adds separate actions, camera framing, weather, and audio for each beat.

output_examples.input: Use an external voice track for lip-sync.
output_examples.output: HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video cannot use external audio for lip-sync. The response recommends a sibling model that accepts audio-driven input.

best_practices: Describe motion over time instead of a still image.
Set aspect ratio, duration, resolution, and audio direction before generation.
Use a short 720P test pass before spending on longer 1080P clips.
anti_patterns: Do not submit sensitive prompts without accepting third-party model processing.
Do not combine many unrelated actions in one short clip.
Do not expect unsupported aspect ratios, long durations, or external audio lip-sync.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It helps generate short text-to-video clips with HappyHorse 1.0 through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill depends on a working RunComfy account, local CLI installation, and authentication.

faq.question: Can it create vertical videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the supported 9:16 aspect ratio and example settings for vertical shorts.

faq.question: Can it use external audio for lip-sync?
faq.answer: No. This template uses in-pass audio only and recommends another model for audio-driven lip-sync.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated outputs into the output directory chosen for the command.

faq.question: Is it safe for private prompts?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prompts are sent to RunComfy model endpoints, so sensitive content should be avoided.
